person.name: Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace
person.summary: Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace, also known as Ada Lovelace, was an English mathematician and writer chiefly known for her work on Charles Babbage's proposed mechanical general-purpose computer, the Analytical Engine. She was the first to recognise that the machine had applications beyond pure calculation and is sometimes considered the first computer programmer.

events.title: Birth of Ada Lovelace
events.description: Augusta Ada Byron was born, the only legitimate child of poet Lord Byron and Anne Isabella Milbanke.

events.title: Ada taken to maternal grandparents' home
events.description: Lady Byron took five-week-old Ada to her parents' home at Kirkby Mallory after separation from Lord Byron.

events.title: Death of Lord Byron
events.description: Ada's father, Lord Byron, died in Greece during the Greek War of Independence.

events.title: Ada's project on flying
events.description: At age 12, Ada began a methodical project to design wings and study flight, including writing a book titled 'Flyology'.

events.title: Meeting Charles Babbage
events.description: Ada met Charles Babbage at one of his Saturday night soirées, beginning a lifelong collaboration and friendship.

events.title: Marriage to William King
events.description: Ada married William, 8th Baron King, becoming Lady King.

events.title: Birth of first child Byron King
events.description: Ada gave birth to her first son, Byron King.

events.title: Husband created Earl of Lovelace
events.description: William King was created Earl of Lovelace and Viscount Ockham, making Ada the Countess of Lovelace.

events.title: Translation and notes on Menabrea's article
events.description: Ada translated Luigi Menabrea's article on the Analytical Engine and added extensive notes, including the first published computer program.

events.title: Publication of notes on Analytical Engine
events.description: Ada's notes were published, describing a method to calculate Bernoulli numbers with the Analytical Engine, considered the first computer program.

events.title: Family's main residence at Horsley Towers
events.description: The family established Horsley Towers as their main home, which Ada helped design.

events.title: Death of Ada Lovelace
events.description: Ada Lovelace died at the age of 36 and was buried next to her father at her request.

events.title: Ada Lovelace commemorated in programming language
events.description: The Ada programming language was named in her honor, recognizing her pioneering contributions to computing.

events.title: Ada Lovelace Day established
events.description: An annual event to celebrate the achievements of women in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) was established on Ada's birthday.
